10.1002_adma.75359: Controlling crystallization kinetics of FAPbI 3 perovskite is crucial for improving crystal quality, device performance and stability. Herein, we report a sustained‐release strategy to regulate the PbI 2 ‐to‐FAPbI 3 conversion. PbI 2 lattice expansion arising from the interaction between PEI (oligomeric poly(ethyleneimine)) and iodide species suppresses nonuniform PbI 2 crystallization and facilitates FAI infiltration. Moreover, the weak interaction between oligomeric PEGDE (poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether) and FAI slows the reaction between FAI and PbI 2 , leading to homogeneous phase conversion during annealing. Consequently, enlarged FAPbI 3 grains are obtained with improved crystallographic orientation, reduced strain and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Furthermore, released PEI and PEGDE undergo in situ crosslinking to form a three‐dimensional network that passivates grain boundaries, stabilizes microstructure and affords inner encapsulation. The resulting champion n‐i‐p device presents a power conversion efficiency of 26.6% (certified 26.17%). Both films and devices exhibit enhanced photothermal stability. The PEI/PEGDE‐treated device maintains 92% of its initial efficiency at 85 °C for over 1,100 h, 96% after continuous illumination (∼100 mW cm − 2 ) and maximum‐power‐point (MPP) tracking for over 1,500 h, and 89% after MPP tracking at 85 °C over 12 days. This work offers a polymerization‐assisted route for synchronizing crystallization control, defect passivation and inner encapsulation to enhance perovskite solar‐cell stability.
10.1002_advs.78449: While the Sabatier-based volcano plots guide catalyst design for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction (HER), the purely thermodynamic hydrogen binding energy descriptor fails to capture experimental HER trends accurately due to the omission of kinetic contributions. Herein, we combine the fixed-potential method with our developed continuous proton supply/consumption model to establish an extra kinetic descriptor for metal-based electrodes (Pt, Pd, Au, Ag, and their bimetallic alloys) under practical working conditions. The potential of zero charge (PZC) is demonstrated to be the interfacial descriptor, which modulates surface charge density and thereby tunes the kinetic proton enrichment within the EDL. Building on this insight, the PZC is integrated with hydrogen binding energies to establish a new two-dimensional volcano plot for HER. The updated volcano plot derived from the dual descriptors effectively matches the experimental results, which provides an additional guiding parameter for rational catalyst design.
10.1016_j.ijdrr.2026.106193: Both coastal and inland flooding affect U.S. communities every year, causing substantial damage to the built environment and long-term socio-economic disruption. To support proactive risk mitigation, this study develops a generalized and scalable framework for building-level, resilience-informed flood risk assessment. The framework integrates FEMA’s National Flood Hazard Layer, fragility-based vulnerability functions, social vulnerability indices, and community resilience factors. A geospatial algorithm is developed to generate coastal and inland flood hazard maps for any U.S. community using FEMA flood data. Building-specific attributes from the National Structure Inventory are used to assign minimal flood archetypes and corresponding depth-damage fragilities to diverse building typologies, enabling high-resolution damage assessment in terms of exceedance probabilities of prescribed damage states. Social vulnerability and community resilience indicators from FEMA’s National Risk Index are incorporated to account for unequal social burdens and adaptive capacity. Machine-learning classification techniques are then applied to categorize buildings into risk-based groups for mitigation prioritization, planning, and investment. Two complementary metrics are produced: a Physical Flood Risk Score reflecting structural damage only, and a Resilience-Informed Risk Score that integrates physical, social, and resilience dimensions into a unified index of community-contextualized flood risk. The framework is demonstrated through a case study of North Carolina using 100-year flood hazard maps at building, census-tract, and county scales.
10.1016_j.microc.2026.118996: The development of electrode materials that combine high capacitance, rapid charge transport, and structural stability remains a central challenge in advancing supercapacitor technology. In this study a ternary nanocomposite copper-doped graphene oxide/polyaniline (Cu–GO/PANI) engineered via novel electrodeposition approach to exploit the synergistic interaction between conducting polymers, two-dimensional carbons, and transition-metal nanoparticles. Structural characterization using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, and field emission scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (FESEM-EDS) confirmed the successful integration of copper nanoparticles within the GO/PANI framework. Electrochemical performance was systematically evaluated by cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The Cu–GO/PANI electrode exhibited a significantly enhanced charge storage capability, achieving a specific capacitance of 1953 F·g⁻¹ at 1 A·g⁻¹, with an energy density of 43.4 Wh·kg⁻¹. The superior performance was attributed to copper-induced doping effects, synergistic interactions between PANI and GO nanosheets, and improved charge-transfer pathways that reduced internal resistance. Although capacitance retention decreased to 53% after 200 cycles, the study demonstrates the effectiveness of this novel synthesis strategy in producing metal–polymer–graphene hybrids. These findings highlight the potential of Cu–GO/PANI as a promising electrode platform for next-generation supercapacitors with high energy and power densities.
